correctness.rationale: The two induced corner families cover all indecomposable projective Lambda-classes because Lambda=eLambda direct-sum fLambda. Inclusion-exclusion gives omega=|A|+|B|-|Lambda|, and the semisimple quotient identifies omega with mixed Wedderburn factors, yielding omega=0 exactly under radical-valued connecting maps. For a tau-rigid direct induction, adjunction identifies all projectives orthogonal to the induced module; inclusion-exclusion then gives |Z|+|P_Z^perp|=|A|+|B|-Delta. The tau-rigid-pair bound yields Delta>=omega, with equality exactly at the support tau-tilting count. The strict M_2(k) example and its finite direct products attain equality with the predicted defect.

originality.rationale: To the best of our knowledge, targeted searches found no prior six-term projective-overlap budget or arbitrary-connecting-map equality criterion for direct support tau-tilting induction. Zhang's 2026 preprint isolates the radical condition as a summand-count hypothesis and supplies the arbitrary-map tau-rigidity test plus an M_2(k) counterexample, but does not state this quantitative replacement. Classical Morita-context radical results are not claimed as novel.

value.rationale: The result converts a qualitative failure of the newest converse theorem outside the radical case into an exact quantitative obstruction and a necessary-and-sufficient criterion. It separates corner support defects, failed projective-side compatibility, and duplicate induced summands, while recovering the radical-valued theorem as the zero-budget case and giving sharp non-radical families.
